subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should OpenClaw add a core trust/provenance model for cron and heartbeat elevated execution, and should it be per-job, scheduling-API based, heartbeat-file metadata based, or folded into the broader scheduling-provenance RFC?
rationale: The source gap is real, but solving it changes who can grant elevated exec to autonomous scheduled work and how existing cron/heartbeat workflows upgrade safely.

options.title: Fold into scheduling provenance RFC
options.body: Use the open non-forgeable scheduling API RFC as the canonical design and make elevated cron/heartbeat trust one requirement of that broader security boundary.

options.title: Narrow per-job elevated flag
options.body: Add a focused cron job provenance/elevated field plus migration and tests while leaving broader agent scheduling API design for later.

options.title: Defer heartbeat trust
options.body: Fix cron provenance first and leave heartbeat elevated behavior behind current `tools.elevated.allowFrom` guidance until a file-edit provenance model exists.

recommendation.title: Fold into scheduling provenance RFC
recommendation.body: Use the open non-forgeable scheduling API RFC as the canonical design and make elevated cron/heartbeat trust one requirement of that broader security boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The adjacent merged cron caller-scope work is the strongest available routing signal for the cron side of this decision.
